rq3_recommendation: Keep the three existing tasks and add one. Priority order. (0) Prerequisite already in hand: object-level accuracy against the four real inventories plus the 400 why verdicts, with a Kmax same-object comparison; reuse it everywhere. (1) NEW: triage a fix commit against a .config (D9). For all objects x 4 configs and the 402 .c/.S commits of v7.2.7..v7.2.8 (a CVE-like proxy, not CVEs), measure false 'not built' (target 0), agreement, commit-level drops, with non-x86 and header-only commits as separate buckets; baselines are Kmax kreader formulas evaluated as kernel-cve-triage does, cvehound's parser if callable, and always-relevant; classify every disagreement and test the kreader-error path; time the whole-tree table against kmaxall on one machine. About 4-6 person-days, minutes of compute. (2) config-for (D2) with three bases (defconfig, Debian with the DLN2 and GPIB requests as worked examples, the syzbot ci config as D11 variant): solved rate, options changed, olddefconfig retention, compile success (reconcile 40 vs 384), failure taxonomy of the 18 with non-x86 split, baselines naive leaf-symbol and predicted allyesconfig plus make file.o; optional klocalizer on about 30 commits only with user approval, one process at a time, smoke test first. (3) blindspots (D4) re-derived with Debian added and composite/intermediate artifacts removed; partition into arch-gated, unreachable under K, actionable; false-blind rate against inventories; 40 stratified actionable objects verified by config-for, olddefconfig and compile; baselines randconfig curve and a Kmax-formula script; fold in the D5 split (undefined symbol / unsat / BROKEN, both Makefile condition and K must over-approximate), checkkconfigsymbols as superset baseline and a 100-defect mutation test. (4) why (D10): counterfactual sufficiency on 100 absent objects per config against baselines nearest-Makefile-symbol, Kmax-formula symbols and why-without-K, with a 50-case hand check of Kconfig-side reasons labelled a limitation. (5) Optional exploratory skip table (D6 plus bisect): per commit and config, commits whose touched objects are all unbuilt, sound only when no header, Kconfig, Makefile or script is touched, with git bisect pathspec and ccache as baselines; do not infer it from the 72 percent figure (289 of 402 commits have at least one, not all, unbuilt object under defconfig). D7 and D3 stay related work and limitations. State up front: object granularity (no #ifdef, headers, toolchain, runtime), x86 entry, K is an over-approximation used only by config-for, no first claim, demand evidenced by policy and operator artifacts rather than surveys. Introduction claims: submit checklist and netdev profile (config choice is the submitter's); krepair 'no assurance' sentence cited once with caveats plus Torvalds 2025; maintainers patching gaps by hand (Golaszewski 2025, Kitt 2022, Hovold 2025, Rini 2022); kernel CNA rule and EU CRA dates for CVE applicability; syzbot ci LLM prompt and manually maintained all_tests.config as operators guessing configs.

open_questions: lore.kernel.org returned HTTP 403 throughout, so all mailing-list evidence comes from partial mirrors and a summarizing fetch tool: no list-wide count of which-CONFIG-builds-X requests, no search for klocalizer or koverage mentions on the lists, no check of 0-day or Kbuild-maintainer statements; claims of the form no maintainer asked for this are unverified, and the web-search budget also ran out so newer competitors may be missing.

No klocalizer or Kmax head-to-head has been run on the same objects: unknown whether kextract's v7.1 parser handles Linux 7.2.8, the default-invocation Kmax runtime and memory on this machine (the saved run used -T and took 6275 s and 28.5 GB), how Kmax treats tristate in the default path, and whether the units-only path ever calls Java.
How Intel 0-day chooses configs per patch is undocumented; if it uses klocalizer or Kmax the novelty of D1, D2 and D6 shrinks.
config_for_compile.json showed 40 sampled commits compiled in one verifier's read while the task statement says 384 verified; reconcile before publishing.

kfold timing is reported as 57.96 s (agreement file), 138.7 s (STATUS.md) and about a minute; the blindspots count of 3,209 includes composite or intermediate artifacts and must be re-derived; the 18 unsolved commits are not split by architecture; the 35 non-.c/.S commits (Rust, DTS, tools, docs) are not characterised; header-only share is 2 percent (krepair) vs 8.8 percent (2022 slides).

Whether the kernel-cve-triage fail-open path (kreader error stored as built=None leading to no file is compiled) triggers in practice is untested; header expansion and multi-arch behaviour were read through a summarizer.

Unverified items: JMake details beyond the DSN abstract, Passos et al. full text, Nguyen and Nguyen 2020 title and venue, PatchLens repository location, Kconfirm and ConfigFix merge status, Debian GPIB amd64 outcome, the 6.12.27 build-fix claim, authors and titles of several PL references.

Stakeholders not heard: Kbuild and Kconfig maintainers, Intel 0-day operators, KernelCI/LKFT/syzbot operators beyond public files, stable maintainers, distro kernel teams, Rust-for-Linux, recent COMPILE_TEST campaign authors; demand is evidenced by policy and operator artifacts only, and the only direct statement of the need is one anonymous LWN comment.

Whether a sound build-condition skip rule yields a non-trivial fraction of skippable commits (bisect or CI matrix) is unmeasured; the 289 of 402 figure counts commits with at least one unbuilt object, not all unbuilt; no Linux-specific prior art on this was found but the search was incomplete.
